name: Multiscale Entropy Analysis
description: Computes sample entropy at multiple time scales to detect complexity differences between real and AI images (Costa et al., 2002).
mechanism:
This method applies Costa et al.'s (2002) Multiscale Entropy (MSE) framework to quantify image complexity across scales:

1. **Coarse-Graining**: The image signal is coarse-grained at multiple temporal scales τ by averaging non-overlapping windows of length τ: yⱼ(τ) = (1/τ)Σᵢ₌₍ⱼ₋₁₎τ₊₁ʲᵗ xᵢ. This creates a family of representations capturing structure at different resolutions.

2. **Sample Entropy Computation**: At each scale τ, sample entropy SampEn(m, r, N) is calculated — measuring the negative natural logarithm of the conditional probability that sequences similar for m points remain similar for m+1 points within tolerance r. This quantifies irregularity without requiring stationarity.

3. **MSE Curve Construction**: The entropy values across scales form the MSE curve. Natural images exhibit a characteristic MSE profile: high entropy at fine scales (sensor noise, texture detail) with controlled decay at coarse scales reflecting structured content.

4. **Complexity Index Computation**: The area under the MSE curve (Complexity Index, CI) provides a single measure of multi-scale complexity. AI-generated images typically show abnormal MSE profiles — either excessively smooth (low MSE across all scales) or with artificial periodicity absent in natural images.

5. **Anomaly Detection**: The MSE curve shape is compared against reference distributions from natural images. Deviations indicate synthetic generation — diffusion models often produce overly regular fine-scale structure, while GANs may show characteristic entropy dips at specific scales corresponding to generator architecture artifacts.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models

references.title: Costa, M. et al. (2002). Multiscale Entropy Analysis of Complex Physiologic Time Series. Physical Review Letters.
Richman, J.S. & Moorman, J.R. (2000). Physiological Time-series Analysis Using Approximate Entropy. AJP Heart.
